steps.title: INTELLLM: LITTLE HINTS MAKE A BIG DIFFERENCE FOR LLM KV CACHE COMPRESSION

core_judgments: The integration of CGE and RGL is presented as a novel solution to the KV cache memory challenge, but the overall novelty of the work is limited.
Sparse attention mechanisms have already been extensively explored in prior literature, such as [1] and [2], which diminishes the originality of the proposed methods.
The CGE component closely resembles previous approaches like H2O [3] and SnapKV [4], with only incremental differences.

conclusion: The submission’s central contribution is IntelLLM, a lightweight, training-free framework for KV‑cache compression that enables efficient long‑text inference via a combination of Center of Gravity Eviction (CGE), Remote Gap Localization (RGL), and a windowing mechanism. However, at the level of this central goal and problem formulation, there is already substantial prior work: GEAR (Zhang et al., 2024), LServe (Jin et al., 2024), RazorAttention (Gomez et al., 2024), Tactic (Gao et al., 2024), and R‑KV (Li et al., 2024) all propose no‑finetuning methods that compress or sparsify the KV cache at inference time to reduce memory/compute while preserving long‑context performance. What the present submission adds beyond these is a specific new eviction policy (CGE, masking the attention “center of gravity” and varying masking/normalization order) and a positional remapping strategy (RGL, shifting distant cache positions to preserve long‑range distinctions within a compression/nearest‑neighbor window design). These mechanisms appear technically distinct and are not found in the examined prior work, but they operate as alternative heuristics within an already well‑explored framework of training‑free KV compression for long‑context LLM serving. Given that this overarching framework is substantially anticipated by prior art, the paper’s novelty is, on balance, not strong enough for a top‑tier venue.
